span.p:
the weakness: in an LCG modulo a power of two,
the low byte evolves entirely on its own —
(s1103515245 + 12345) mod 256 == (low0x6D + 0x39) mod 256

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 560px; text-align: center;

span.p:
that map is a single 256-long cycle, so every
record's keystream is one of only 256 sequences,
identified by its phase. The junk bytes are the
other generator's low byte, from the same cycle.

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 560px; text-align: center;

span.p:
at junk positions: packed[p] = cycle[a+p] ^ cycle[b+p]
at real positions: packed[p] = code ^ cycle[a+p]
-> vote over all positions to recover a and b

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 560px; text-align: center;

span.p:
b comes from the master key alone, so it is the
same for every record: 243. A free consistency
check across all 1035 decodes.

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 560px; text-align: center;

span.p:
but this still isn't exact. When a real code byte
happens to equal the junk byte it would take, a run of
junk looks one byte longer and the walk loses sync —
yielding clean, plausible, wrong x86-64.

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 560px; text-align: center;

span.p:
so recover the junk generator's full 32-bit state,
not just its low byte. 24 bits left, one unambiguous
record to check against, a few seconds of brute force:
dejunk seed = 0x429057CE

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 560px; text-align: center;

span.p:
the generator restarts identically for every record,
so the skip pattern is global — real bytes always sit
at the same offsets. Every record now decodes exactly.

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 560px; text-align: center;

span.p:
1034 clean x86-64 functions, each ending in ret,
plus record 9990, which is 40 bytes of data

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 560px; text-align: center;

span.p:
each function takes a byte in rcx and a 32-byte state
in rdx, stirs four state bytes, burns a million-iteration
delay loop whose sum is subtracted straight back off,
and returns the id of the next function to run

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 560px; text-align: center;

span.p:
start at id 52090, state all zeros.
Only 1035 of 2^32 returns name a real record, so at
almost every step exactly one input byte keeps it alive.

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 560px; text-align: center;

span.p:
depth-first over the 256 bytes, printable first:
FLAREON_ASN1_Labyrinth_Key_2026! — 31 steps, id 4485

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 560px; text-align: center;
display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 560px; text-align: center;

span.p:
